bullets.title: TSMC records all-time high June revenue; Q2 beats top-end of guidance
bullets.body: TSMC June revenue hit NT$442.68B, up 67.9% YoY and 6.2% MoM—a new all-time high surpassing the prior record of NT$417B set in May 2026. Q2 2026 revenue reached NT$1.27T ($40.07B), up 36% YoY to a record quarterly high, driven by strong AI chip production demand. H1 2026 revenue rose 35.6% to NT$2.40T.

bullets.title: TSMC capacity expansion: 1.4nm ahead of schedule, 3 more advanced packaging plants planned
bullets.body: TSMC's 1.4nm fab is 'far ahead of schedule'—first fab finishes April 2027, pilot production in Q3 2027, mass production targeted mid-2028. Additionally, TSMC plans 3 new advanced packaging plants at Chiayi Science Park Phase II, bringing the total to 5. Also reportedly plans a single-digit price hike on mature-process chips effective January 2027.

bullets.title: TSMC facing CoWoS capacity crunch; orders spilling to Intel
bullets.body: TSMC cannot meet CoWoS advanced packaging demand, forcing overflow orders to Intel and rival Taiwanese fabs. Google Pixel 11 (Tensor G6), Apple A20, and MediaTek are all on TSMC's 2nm process in Q3-Q4 2024.

bullets.title: NVDA: Anthropic compute share rises to ~50% on Nvidia; Rubin delay confirmed
bullets.body: NVIDIA disclosed at a Morgan Stanley NDR that Anthropic's share of compute running on its chips has risen to nearly 50%. Separately, expert call indicates NVIDIA's Rubin architecture has been delayed again; Micron reportedly failed on original Rubin pin specs, prompting NVIDIA to lower targets to enable ecosystem shipments.

bullets.title: MU: HBM4E bit exchange rate 4-5x DRAM premium; 2027 worst memory supply year per SK Hynix CEO
bullets.body: SK Hynix CEO warns 2027 will be the worst year for memory supply in industry history, with demand expected to outpace capacity for the next decade. One analyst notes HBM4E bit exchange rate is 4-5x higher than standard DRAM, with further premiums anticipated in HBM5/HBM5E—a dynamic the market underappreciates, especially for Micron.

bullets.title: Goldman: hyperscaler capex may exceed $360B credit window; 'carnage' in hyperscaler bonds
bullets.body: Goldman FICC strategist Jeffery Papai warned that credit investors are signaling difficulty funding another $360B in the next 12 months via existing methods, against ~$1T in hyperscaler capex needs. Big Tech debt has doubled to $350B over five years funding AI data centers; hyperscaler capex now equals 100% of cash flow.

bullets.title: META up 11% in two days; Muse Spark 1.1 gaining attention; capex plans intact
bullets.body: META shares rose 11% over two trading days, the best two-day gain since April 2025, reaching 19% gains in July. Muse Spark 1.1 benchmark results on LMArena are prompting talk of multi-bagger upside potential, with one fintwit account describing META as 'severely underpriced' at current Polymarket odds. Meta's next-year capex resists cut fears per weekly wrap.

bullets.title: Meta chip push: AVGO's Iris prototype completed in 6 months; Qualcomm and MediaTek in loop
bullets.body: Meta is collaborating with Qualcomm and MediaTek on new ASIC projects, using Qualcomm CPUs and working with Arm. Broadcom completed the 'Iris' chip prototype in 6 months and is in testing phase. Meta also halted its AI image tool for public Instagram profiles amid backlash.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure bull/bear: MAG7 at cheapest relative P/E since 2016; insider buying record
bullets.body: MAG7 relative P/E vs S&P 500 dropped to 1.17x, lowest in a decade vs 10-year avg of 1.53x. Tech insider buying hit the fastest pace ever. MSFT expected to grow earnings 64% over next 3 years despite 23% YTD decline. CEOs of MSFT, PLTR, NVDA share synchronized bull thesis on AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: US-Iran escalation slams AI stocks; KOSPI falls 8.95% triggering circuit breaker
bullets.body: AI-related stocks slid globally as US struck Iran for the third time in a week and Iran claimed closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Oil surged 4%, Treasury yields rose, and 2-year yields hit 4.23%—highest since February 2025. South Korea's KOSPI crashed 8.95% to a circuit-breaker halt; Korean stocks now at historic valuation lows while SK Hynix's US ADR fell 10.4% premarket.

bullets.title: 30-year real yield hits 2.9%, highest since GFC; bond market structural warning
bullets.body: U.S. 30-year real rates rose to 2.9%, the highest since the Global Financial Crisis. The 2-year Treasury yield jumped above 4.23%, a 17-month high. Sticky inflation from the Iran oil shock is firming expectations for further Fed hikes per NY Fed President Williams (threshold: 0.2% monthly core CPI). U.S. dollar share of global FX reserves hit lowest level this century.

bullets.title: AAPL sues OpenAI for trade secret theft; 400 Apple employees recruited
bullets.body: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging misappropriation of trade secrets, including that OpenAI's chief hardware officer directed former Apple staff to bring confidential hardware components. OpenAI has hired approximately 400 people from Apple. AAPL reached record highs in July amid AI momentum.

bullets.title: AAPL: tariff exemption secured in exchange for manufacturing chips at Intel fabs
bullets.body: WSJ reports Apple secured an exemption from semiconductor tariffs in exchange for committing to manufacture both Mac and iPhone chips at Intel fabs—significant for INTC's foundry utilization outlook.

bullets.title: SNDK: Goldman raises PT to $3,100; three NBM agreements signed in FQ3
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs raised SanDisk's price target to $3,100 (upside to $4,000) citing recently signed New Business Model agreements. Three NBMs signed in FQ3 with ~$42B of RPO plus two additional committed. Bottleneck trade outperformed SNDK and Hynix until LTA details were clarified.

bullets.title: AMD: vLLM optimization re-prioritized after ROCm support removed; Radeon MFG 8x quietly added
bullets.body: AMD engineers are re-prioritizing vLLM after ROCm support was removed from the vime framework; performance improvements expected. AMD Radeon drivers quietly added Multi Frame Generation 'MFG 8x' and Ray Regeneration features, hinting at a bigger FSR push. On benchmarks, NVIDIA's B300 outperforms B200 and 'mogs' AMD on vLLM Kimi.

bullets.title: Grok 4.5 reaches Opus-class browser performance; accelerating fastest among AI models
bullets.body: Elon Musk and observers note Grok 4.5 improved from 6/33 to 23/33 on video studio evaluations and now ties for #1 on SWE-Atlas-QnA. Grok 4.5 also ranked slightly above Fable on software benchmarks and is described as 'accelerating the fastest' among current AI models. Tesla and SpaceX staff asked to evaluate Grok 4.5.

bullets.title: TSLA FSD praised; Cybercab at fork in road; Optimus demonstrations quiet down
bullets.body: Retail users describe Tesla FSD as 'greatest piece of technology' experienced. Tesla Megapack hits 10 GWh operational in Australia. However, one skeptical account notes Tesla has reduced public Optimus robot demonstrations and questions whether noise-cancelling-via-speakers feature was delivered.

bullets.title: HOOD: Robinhood Chain sees $633M DEX volume; 70K+ Agentic Trading accounts opened
bullets.body: Robinhood Chain DEX volume hit $633M with 306.5k daily active users. ETH bridged to Robinhood Chain surged ~70x in a week to exceed $70M. Separately, Robinhood reports more than 70,000 Agentic Trading accounts opened since May launch, expanding to crypto. CEO touts Trump Accounts for 'skin in the game from birth.'

bullets.title: TSMC CPO lead over Samsung confirmed; silicon photonics testing bottleneck rising
bullets.body: PhotonCap field research concludes TSMC is ahead in CPO (chiplet-on-package) technology; Samsung developing a 2.xD multi-chip package binding HBM, logic, and a third chip together (disclosed at Nano Korea). Silicon photonics testing is becoming the dominant bottleneck alongside packaging as AI and advanced packaging scale.

bullets.title: China halts helium exports amid Qatar outage; US semiconductor imports from Taiwan surpass China
bullets.body: China halted helium exports as US-Iran tensions threaten chip supply. Separately, Taiwan has replaced China as the third-largest US import source in the last 6 months, driven by advanced semiconductor imports that touched $100B in May for only the second time ever.
